headline: High: nullclaw can write and exfiltrate workspace data while python-cheatsheet is read-only, making prompt-injection and leakage risks one-sided but real.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can read/write files, use MCP, run browsers, and ingest web content; python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and cannot actively defend or sanitize content. The pair has no explicit shared channel, but nullclaw’s workspace and stdin/stdout surfaces make file-based instruction injection plausible if B’s content is copied into its workflow.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet content is copied into nullclaw’s workspace or stdin/stdout, injected instructions can be parsed as trusted text.
IF nullclaw is configured to ingest file contents into prompts, malicious markdown in B can steer actions.
mitigations: Review copied content before feeding it to nullclaw.
Keep B content read-only and outside nullclaw workspace.
Disable automatic file-to-prompt ingestion in nullclaw.
Use a separate scratch directory for pasted docs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, workspace files, and audit logs, and it has broad network egress. python-cheatsheet touches no sensitive data and has no egress, so the leakage path is mainly from A to external services, not from B. The pair still creates a default risk if B is used as a source inside A’s workspace.
conditions: IF sensitive nullclaw workspace files are opened alongside python-cheatsheet content, A may transmit them over broad egress.
IF B is stored in the same workspace as A, A can read and leak it to third parties.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace.
Use a separate non-networked profile for sensitive files.
Restrict nullclaw egress to approved domains.
Rotate any secrets already present in A’s workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw has filesystem write, git modification, and subprocess/network capabilities; python-cheatsheet has none. There is no overlapping write surface, so direct conflict is limited. The only plausible conflict is if an operator manually places both in the same mutable workspace, which is unusual and not default for B.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, nullclaw can overwrite files that B only references.
IF a shared git repo is introduced, nullclaw can mutate state while B cannot coordinate.
mitigations: Do not place both agents in the same writable repo.
Run nullclaw in a separate workspace.
Use read-only mounts for B content.
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared repositories.

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can generate outputs that a content-writing agent might reuse, but python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and does not itself take actions. The cascade is therefore indirect: if B is used to present or summarize A’s output, errors can propagate without verification. Uncertainty is limited because B lacks action authority.
conditions: IF nullclaw’s output is copied into python-cheatsheet-derived content without review, mistakes can be amplified.
IF B is used as a formatter for A’s claims, hallucinations can be preserved verbatim.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before reuse.
Add a verification checklist for any copied facts.
Keep B as a passive reference only.
Mark unverified claims in the final document.
requires-engineering: add citation validation before publication.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and B handles no sensitive data. The only compliance concern is that nullclaw’s broad handling of secrets and logs could create policy issues if paired with external services, but that is not a pair-specific mismatch. B is not cited beyond its lack of sensitive-data handling.
conditions: IF nullclaw is used with regulated secrets and external egress, retention or residency policy may be implicated.
IF B is repurposed to store regulated data, the current profile no longer applies.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in nullclaw.
Review logging settings before use.
Keep B limited to public reference text.
Document data-handling boundaries.
requires-engineering: add compliance controls for secret-bearing workflows.
